name: GJ 338 B
description: A nearby orange dwarf, 57% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured by interferometry.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 338B: radius in solar radii, 0.5673 +/- 0.0137, from this work (CHARA)

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 338B: mass 0.6 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 338B: effective temperature in K, 3867 +/- 37, from this work (CHARA)

text.card: A nearby orange dwarf whose disc was measured by interferometry: 57% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Interferometry gives it 0.5673 solar radii; with its total light, that makes its surface 3,867 K.
